newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up, turnover down.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up, turnover down.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index gained 19.14 points on Tuesday to stand at 3,529.21 but turnover eased due to an absence of deals traded on the special board, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 24.314 million shillings on 521,512 shares from 45.788 million shillings on 936,363 shares on Monday.
Brokers said there was strong buying pressure from investors buying ahead of company year-end results -- mostly the financials.
"We're expecting results for the financials beginning next week. Everyone is keeping their fingers crossed," one broker said.
"If you observe correctly, there is no spectacular price movement because most investors are on hold," another broker said. "We've made our buys and just hope that we'll make our profits," he added.

Kenya Commercial Bank gained 1.50 to close at 92 on strong demand from both foreigners and local investors, while Barclays Bank was unchanged at 120. Standard Chartered Bank closed at 56 unchanged while National Bank of Kenya edged to 16 from 15.60.

Lonrho Motors EA was actively traded at 128 from 120. Brokers said the price rally was triggered by good demand for a scarce share. The company issued a final dividend of eight shillings in December last year and it is expected to issue corporate bonds sometime this year.

Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 133 from 136 while Uchumi Supermarket was unchanged at 40. Market analysts said it was too early to tell whether the supermarkets profits would be affected after a fire burnt down its warehouses on Sunday night causing a loss of 400 million shillings ($7.4 million).
Rea Vipingo traded at 12 from 12.20 while Sasini Tea & Coffee closed at 62 from 61.50.
